title: Medical Vault Document Envelope, version 1
description: Describes one source document (a photograph or scan of a medical result) and the provenance of everything derived from it. Written once, never mutated. Corrections are recorded as a new envelope whose `supersedes` names the one it replaces.

document_id.description: ULID. Lexicographically sortable by creation time, so a plain directory listing is chronological.

subject_id.description: The person the document is about. A tenant may hold records for several people.

supersedes.description: document_id of an envelope this one corrects. The superseded record is never deleted.

captured_at.description: When the medical event happened, as printed on the document. This is the clinically meaningful time.

recorded_at.description: When this record entered the vault. Distinct from captured_at: a 2019 report may be filed in 2031.

document_type.description: Free text, not an enum. An enum here would need a code change to file a kind of report nobody has thought of yet. Conventional values: blood_panel, ultrasound, radiology, pathology, prescription, discharge_summary, vaccination, vitals, other.

filename.description: Name of the original file as stored beside this envelope.

sha256.description: Digest of the original bytes. Lets a future reader prove the image was never altered.

provider.description: Where the test was done. Kept as written, including the original script.

name_raw.description: Verbatim, e.g. 上海电力医院

name_en.description: Translation, e.g. Shanghai Electric Power Hospital

accession.description: The lab's own identifier for this report.

language.description: BCP 47 tag of the document's primary language, as detected.

extraction.description: How the structured data was obtained. Recorded so an extraction can be reproduced, audited, or re-run with a better model years later.

review.description: Human verification. An AI extraction is a draft until a person confirms it; analytics can filter on this.

narrative.description: Prose sections that are not measurements: findings, impressions, clinical history. Preserved in the original language with a translation alongside, because the wording of an impression carries meaning that a code cannot.

notes.description: Free text added by the owner.
